newsitem.title: USA: Insurance industry facing major changes.
newsitem.headline: Insurance industry facing major changes.

text.p: The Internet, the capital markets and competition from banks will bring about profound changes in the insurance industry in the next decade, speakers at a Coopers & Lybrand insurance conference said on Tuesday.
Companies that succeed in the 21st century will be those that respond to these and other changes taking place in the industry, the speakers said.
"The Internet is going to have a profound impact on the way we sell insurance," CNA Financial Corp chief executive Dennis Chookaszian said.
He said the Internet would be a significant factor in the sale of auto, homeowners and some term insurance.
William Bolinder, member of the corporate executive board at the Zurich Insurance Co, urged insurance executives to start implementing the Internet in their businesses now.

"It's not really ready for prime time but don't, I repeat, don't, underestimate it," Bolinder said, speaking earlier at the Coopers & Lybrand's eighth annual executive conference for the property/casualty industry. "I highly recommend you get yourselves involved quickly," he said.
The capital markets also will bring about big changes in the insurance industry, the speakers said.
The capital markets will not replace the insurance industry, but "the capital markets are going to be part of it," Bolinder said.
And the insurance industry will need the capital markets, the speakers said.
"It has to work. There isn't enough capital in the insurance industry to meet the long-term needs," said Michael Butt, chief executive of Mid Ocean Ltd's Mid Ocean Reinsurance Co Ltd.
But capital market alternatives have had little success recently, partly because of soft reinsurance prices.
"I think we have to be attentive," said Herbert Haag, chief executive of Partner Reinsurance Ltd PTREF.O.
"Unfortunately, the present weak pricing climate is not helping the capital markets," making reinsurance a more attractive alternative.
But CNA's Chookaszian said "securitization will happen to the insurance industry."
Banks also will play a major role in changing the insurance industry, Chookaszian said.

Although banks are already selling insurance they are not likely to pose a major competitive threat in insurance underwriting. However, they are likely to become a major new distribution channel, Chookaszian said.
He said he expects to see banks form partnerships with independent insurance agencies to sell insurance.
"That will become one of the key distribution mechanisms," he said.
